terms.gloss: a layer laid down: of mortar, sand, earth
evidence: Cato Agr. 18.7: prīmum corium facitō … alterum corium (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its first sense is skin, hide or leather; in building it is a layer laid on a surface, as in Cato’s floors and Vitruvius’s plaster, and Pliny uses it of a layer of earth. So it suits a layer that is put down or built up.

terms.gloss: a hard surface layer, a crust; a coating or facing
evidence: Verg. G. 3.360: fluminis, a crust of ice on a river (Lewis & Short)
Plin. NH 35.154: parietis, a facing on a wall (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A layer that covers: the crust of bread, a skin of ice, a marble facing. Also a scab (see scab).

terms.gloss: a storey, a floor; of branches or fruit, a layer, tier
evidence: Col. 12.39.3 (Lewis & Short): grapes laid in layers
terms.comment: Properly boarding and a storey of a building or a tower; Vergil and Columella use it of the tiers of a tree’s branches and of fruit laid in rows.

phrases.latin: ubi lībrāveris, dē glāreā et calce harēnātō prīmum corium facitō, id pīlīs subigitō, idem alterum corium facitō
phrases.english: when you have levelled it, make a first layer of gravel and lime mortar, ram it down with pestles, and make a second layer the same way

sources: Lewis & Short: corium · Lewis & Short: crusta · Lewis & Short: tabulatus
